problem: Existing omni-modal models and VLN agents treat audio as mono semantic input and ignore spatial acoustic cues (direction, distance), and there is no real-world benchmark or scalable geometry-consistent training data for spatial audio-visual reasoning and sound-guided navigation.
motivation: Humans use sound to localize occluded or off-screen targets and to guide search, so embodied agents should too. Real spatial-audio data is costly to collect, and simulated audio must stay geometrically consistent with vision and agent motion. Pretrained omni models lack a way to integrate FOA spatial audio without hurting their semantic audio ability.
key_idea: Graft a pretrained FOA spatial encoder onto Qwen3-Omni alongside its frozen semantic audio tower, train it on geometry-consistent rendered FOA QA and sound-augmented VLN data, and evaluate it on a new real-world FOA benchmark (OmniEchoBench).
insight: Spatial and semantic audio are complementary: removing the native audio tower drops Overall from 28.5 to 26.2, and the FOA encoder lifts source-centric tasks (Direction, 3D localization, Motion, Cognitive Map) but not camera rotation, which depends on vision. Dedicated Stage-1/2 pretraining and freezing the encoder in Stage 3 matter: unfreezing drops Overall to 26.2, and adding an untrained FOA encoder gives no clear gain. Navigation failures come mainly from stopping and distance estimation: GT direction raises SR from 16.2 to 23.7 and SPL from 11.5 to 22.1, and 36.67% of episodes enter the goal region without stopping. Fine-tuning on a small amount of real data raises QA Overall from 28.5 to 34.9, indicating a sim-to-real gap.
method: FOA feature encoder: an ~11.9M-parameter conv-Transformer over a 5-channel map (log-mel of W, DirAC intensity ix/iy/iz, diffuseness) producing 384-d tokens at ~12.5 tokens/s.
Stage 1 semantic alignment: align pooled clip embeddings to frozen CLIP text embeddings with a class-balanced SigLIP-style sigmoid loss on 100k synthetic FOA clips (644 labels).
Stage 2 query-conditioned localization: a cross-attention head predicts (sin/cos azimuth, sin/cos elevation, log distance) given a text query, with the semantic loss kept as a regularizer.

Stage 3 dual-path integration into Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B: W-channel mono goes to the frozen audio tower, and FOA spatial tokens pass through a trainable projector (384→2048→2048) into <foa_pad> slots inserted after the audio tokens; only the LLM and projector are trained.

Spatial audio-visual data synthesis: an LLM director scripts scenes, Seedance generates video and per-source stems, source geometry is recovered from the rendered video, stems are encoded to FOA (Eq. 1) with off-screen sources and camera yaw added, and QA pairs are computed from trajectories (26.6k AV QA and 18.5k audio QA).

Sound-guided navigation data: R2R/RxR/VLN-PE/ScaleVLN episodes get a VLM-proposed destination sound (TTS speech or Seedance events) rendered as FOA with distance attenuation, reverberation and optional noise, with CoT rationales, in-place turning and stop supervision; the model outputs K=8 waypoints.

OmniEchoBench: QA over 197 real FOA recordings (2,972 QA: source direction, 3D localization, source motion, camera rotation, plus a 600-question cognitive-map task) and Nav over 30 scanned scenes with a dense FOA acoustic field (900 samples, 12,900 recordings) for closed-loop Habitat evaluation.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B Thinker (LLM fine-tuned) + trainable projector + frozen FOA encoder, audio tower and visual tower
setting.training_data: 363,193 examples in Stage 3: navigation from ScaleVLN 139,142, RxR 92,418, R2R 31,577, VLN-PE 28,969, plus 25,984 in-place rotation, 26,585 spatial AV QA and 18,518 audio QA; the FOA encoder is pretrained on 100k synthetic FOA clips
setting.observation: egocentric RGB history frames (up to 8 plus the current one) + 4-channel FOA audio (+ text instruction); no depth
setting.action_space: K=8 relative waypoints [x_fwd, y_left, yaw] converted to discrete actions (stop, forward 0.25 m, turn 15°)
setting.simulator: Habitat (real-scanned meshes for OmniEchoBench-Nav; VLN-CE R2R with simulated FOA)
setting.privileged: none for the main results (the GT-direction variant is an analysis only); the nearest-receiver recording from the pre-captured acoustic field is used as the audio observation in OmniEchoBench-Nav

numbers.eval_set_note: held-out scenario-disjoint test part after using 1,000 real samples for training
numbers.extra: fine-tuned on 1,000 real benchmark samples; the table's first row is the synthetic-only model

results: OmniEcho reaches 28.5 Overall on OmniEchoBench-QA (audio+vision), beating Qwen3-Omni (18.5) and SO-7B (11.4). On sound-guided navigation it gets 16.2 SR / 11.5 SPL on OmniEchoBench-Nav, above Seq2Seq and CMA but below InternVLA-N1 (17.8 / 16.7). On VLN-CE R2R with audio only it gets 22.2 SR, comparable to Seq2Seq and CMA but far below InternVLA-N1 (50.6).
limitations: Sim-to-real gap remains: training is on synthetic data, and adding real data lifts QA Overall from 28.5 to 34.9. Fine-grained localization and distance estimation are weak (3D localization 14.2, distance Pearson r 0.27).
Poor stopping and path efficiency: 52.89% of episodes reach the goal region but only 16.22% succeed, and it trails strong text-guided VLN systems.
Navigation is evaluated in simulation over a pre-captured discrete receiver grid (nearest-receiver audio), and real-robot evidence is only qualitative.
